exceptions.justification: CVE-2026-16742 is reported by Trivy against libsystemd0 in the Debian bookworm base with no fixed version available, so there is no patched package to upgrade to and the finding cannot be cleared by rebuilding. It is accepted here on reachability rather than on any claim about the flaw itself. This container does not run systemd: its PID 1 is the postgres entrypoint started from the Compose command, there is no init system, no journald, no logind and no dbus, and libsystemd0 is present only as a transitive link brought in by Debian packaging rather than as a service anything executes. The service is also unreachable from outside the appliance: it publishes no host port, is attached only to the internal backend and monitoring networks, runs read_only with cap_drop ALL and no-new-privileges, and is addressed solely as postgres:5432 by other containers. Accepted for this release only, expiring in three months so it returns for review rather than persisting silently. Re-check whether bookworm has released a fixed libsystemd0 before renewing. Carried forward to 1.4.1 on 2026-09-20: 1.4.1 is a fix release that changes no Dockerfile and no pinned image input, so the Debian base carrying this package is byte-for-byte the one reviewed for 1.4.0 and the reachability argument above is unchanged. The expiry is deliberately not extended with the carry-forward; it still falls on 2026-12-08, so the finding returns for a fresh decision on its own schedule rather than on the release cadence. Carried forward again to 1.4.2 on 2026-09-20: 1.4.2 changes one host shell script and re-pins two vendored application trees whose bytes were already identical. It touches no Dockerfile, no pinned package version and no Debian snapshot, so the postgres image this finding is reported against is byte-for-byte the one reviewed for 1.4.0, and the reachability argument is unchanged. The expiry is still not extended and still falls on 2026-12-08. Carried forward again to 1.4.3 on 2026-09-20: 1.4.3 changes only Status TypeScript source and the release version fields. The expiry is still not extended and still falls on 2026-12-08. Same finding as the libsystemd0 entry, reported a second time against libudev1, which ships from the same Debian systemd source package and is likewise unfixed in bookworm. The reasoning is identical and no weaker: libudev1 is a device-enumeration library, this container runs no udev daemon and enumerates no devices, its only storage is a Docker volume mounted at /var/lib/postgresql/data, and the service publishes no host port and sits only on the internal backend and monitoring networks. Present as a transitive link, never executed. Accepted for this release only, expiring in three months so it returns for review rather than persisting silently. Re-check whether bookworm has released a fixed systemd source package before renewing.
